title: The Wise Men of Chelm, the Challah and the Goat
summary: Avreml of Chelm buys a golden challah for Shabbat and suddenly gets stuck: which side do you cut a challah from? He asks Reb Kalman, Reb Zalman and Reb Shmerel, and each one gives a different answer. Then, while nobody is watching, a white goat with a little bell comes along... and everyone discovers the answer. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
Avreml of Chelm bought a challah for Shabbat, plump and fat,
golden and shiny, full of sesame, smelling of joy at that.
He took a knife in his hand — and froze, and stood, eyes open wide:
"Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side?
That's a big, big, BIG question to decide!"

Avreml ran to Reb Kalman, holding the challah like a pot,
"From the right!" he answered, "Right is honor — clear as a song, is it not?"
"Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side?
That's a big, big, BIG question to decide!"

Avreml ran to Reb Zalman, the tall one, and asked the same thing,
"From the left!" said Zalman, "That's where the heart is — the challah's heart, the main thing!"
"Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side?
That's a big, big, BIG question to decide!"

Reb Shmerel raised a finger and said, "From the middle! In the middle all sides are the same,
and the challah stays as if still whole — every side whole, just as it came!"
"Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side?
That's a big, big, BIG question to decide!"

Avreml turned the challah right, then left, then up and down,
and asked it gently — but a challah doesn't answer in any language in town.
"Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side?
That's a big, big, BIG question to decide!"

The sun went slowly down, and Avreml sat on the bench, shut his eyes and thought,
the challah on his knees, the thought so big and deep, and time went by a lot.
And behind the fence, on the tips of her hooves, came a white goat with a little bell,
she peeked, and sniffed, and said to herself, "What a sweet smell!"

The goat stretched out her neck and opened her mouth, big and round,
and NOM! NOM! NOM! — ate a whole side of the challah, right down to the ground!

Avreml opened his eyes, and instead of getting mad — he laughed out loud:
"Now I know — from the goat's side, I can say it proud!"
"Which side do you cut a challah from? From the goat's side!
That's a big, big, BIG answer, far and wide!"

The wise men came and heard, and clapped their hands with glee:
"There's a wise goat in Chelm — she teaches all the heavens, even they agree!"
And Reb Shmerel raised a finger: "From now on every challah starts with a goat — that's my decree!"

And in the evening, on the table, the candles glowed, and the challah, half a challah, lay on its plate,
and the goat? She got a little slice — because goats love Shabbat too, and think it's great.

And all of Chelm heard, and in every home on Friday night a white goat stood by,
and the challah — after her first bite — was ready, and nobody asked why.

And next Friday Avreml bought a challah, big and fat,
and politely offered it to the goat, and asked, "Which side do you cut a challah from? Which side is that?"
"Maa-a-a!" answered the goat — and NOM! —
That's a big, big, BIG answer, and that's that!
